note: Kaggle serve candidates for T0. status 'unmeasured' means nothing was run and every number is null. status 'partial' means a real sysop serve session was timed (time_to_healthy_s, measured_on) but tok_s is null: spikes/kaggle_probe.py was not run (no key could be had without reading a credential file), so the speed is kept in tok_s_sysop with its provenance (sysop's models.json, dated 2026-10-06 in tok_s_measured_on). measured_on dates time_to_healthy_s only (2026-11-01). 'measured' needs every field. Do not fill a field from a guess. 'serve' holds the llama-server configuration the endpoint serves (slots, per-slot ctx, flags). The time_to_healthy_s figures were measured with sysop's 2 slots of 32768 config (SERVE_SLOTS 2, SERVE_CTX 32768) for all three models: the 35B is served with that config, and the 27B and gemma are served at 2 slots of 16384, a conservative pick with no run of its own. The tok_s_sysop figures were measured with sysop's 8 slots of 4096 throughput benchmark config, not with 'serve'. Each serve.source says which is which.

single_model_both_t4.tok_s_source: sysop reference scripts/kaggle/models.json tok_s (111.1), whose own source line reads 'sysop batch 2026-10-06: 2x T4, 8 parallel, 48x256 tokens of code, llama.cpp CUDA q8_0 KV'; measured by sysop on 2026-10-06, not by spikes/kaggle_probe.py and not re-measured on 2026-11-01
single_model_both_t4.time_to_healthy_source: ready_s printed by sysop serve up, measured by sysop serve (sysop.py serve up/list) on 2026-11-01, not by spikes/kaggle_probe.py
single_model_both_t4.notes: context and VRAM not reported by sysop serve; left null. The plan's free-kaggle id qwen3.6-35b-a3b is served by sysop under this id.

serve.source: sysop reference scripts/kaggle/models.json entry qwen3.6-35b-a3b (flags unchanged from that entry: -ngl 99 --split-mode layer --flash-attn on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0). time_to_healthy_s (221 s, 2026-11-01) was measured by sysop serve with this same config (SERVE_SLOTS 2, SERVE_CTX 32768): 2 x 32768 is the context sysop's agent jobs ran on this model with the same flags, so it is the measured agent context, not a guess. tok_s_sysop (111.1, 2026-10-06) was measured with the 8 slots of 4096 throughput benchmark config, which refuses any request over 4096 tokens (exceed_context_size_error); pi's own system prompt was measured at about 1600 tokens live on 2026-11-11, from pi's own request, and leaves no room for the task under 4096. So the tok/s of the served config is UNMEASURED in this repo. llama-server gets --parallel 2 and -c 65536, as in the reference scripts/kaggle/common.py.
